items.title: Weakly closed nonlinear forward maps on Hilbert spaces

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems, Chapter 10

items.statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $D\subseteq X$ be nonempty, and let $F:D\to Y$ be a forward map. The domain $D$ is **weakly closed** when it is closed in the weak topology $\sigma(X,X^*)$, the coarsest topology making every bounded real-linear functional on $X$ continuous. The graph of $F$ is **sequentially weak-to-weak closed** when, for every sequence $(x_n)$ in $D$ and every $x\in X$ and $z\in Y$, the conditions $x_n\rightharpoonup x$ and $F(x_n)\rightharpoonup z$ imply $x\in D$ and $F(x)=z$; here weak convergence means convergence under every bounded real-linear functional on the corresponding Hilbert space. We call $F$ a **weakly closed forward map** when its domain is weakly closed and its graph is sequentially weak-to-weak closed. No linearity, norm continuity, Fréchet differentiability, or convexity is assumed; linear maps are allowed as special cases.

items.title: The nonlinear Tikhonov functional

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems, equation (10.1)

items.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $D\subseteq X$ be a nonempty domain, and let $F:D\to Y$ be a forward map. For a regularization parameter $\alpha>0$, reference element $x_0\in X$, and datum $y\in Y$, the **nonlinear Tikhonov functional** is the map $J_{\alpha,y,x_0}:D\to[0,\infty)$ defined by

$$
J_{\alpha,y,x_0}(x):=\frac12\|F(x)-y\|_Y^2+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|x-x_0\|_X^2\qquad(x\in D).
$$

A **global minimizer** is a point $x_\alpha\in D$ such that $J_{\alpha,y,x_0}(x_\alpha)\le J_{\alpha,y,x_0}(x)$ for every $x\in D$. This definition asserts neither existence nor uniqueness.

items.title: $x_0$-minimum-norm solutions on weakly closed domains

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems, Chapter 10
Benedikt Wirth, Inverse Problems, Definition 83 and Theorem 85

items.statement:
Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $D\subseteq X$ be nonempty and weakly closed, meaning closed in the coarsest topology making every bounded real-linear functional continuous, and let $F:D\to Y$ satisfy this graph condition: whenever $x_n\in D$, $x_n\rightharpoonup x$, and $F(x_n)\rightharpoonup z$, one has $x\in D$ and $F(x)=z$; weak convergence means convergence under every bounded real-linear functional. For $x_0\in X$ and $y\in Y$, a point $x^\dagger\in D$ is an **$x_0$-minimum-norm solution** of $F(x)=y$ when $F(x^\dagger)=y$ and

$$
\|x^\dagger-x_0\|_X\le\|x-x_0\|_X\qquad\text{for every }x\in D\text{ with }F(x)=y.
$$

This definition asserts neither existence nor uniqueness. The minimum is global over the exact solution set in $D$ and uses distance from the specified reference point $x_0$.

items.title: The exact solution set of a weakly closed map is weakly sequentially closed

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems, Chapter 10

items.statement: Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $D\subseteq X$ be nonempty and weakly closed, meaning closed in the coarsest topology making every bounded real-linear functional continuous, and let $F:D\to Y$ satisfy this graph condition: whenever $x_n\in D$, $x_n\rightharpoonup x$, and $F(x_n)\rightharpoonup z$, one has $x\in D$ and $F(x)=z$. Weak convergence means convergence under every bounded real-linear functional. For $y\in Y$, the exact solution set $S_F(y):=\{x\in D:F(x)=y\}$ is weakly sequentially closed in $X$: every sequence in $S_F(y)$ that converges weakly to $x$ has $x\in S_F(y)$.

items.title: Existence of a global nonlinear Tikhonov minimizer

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems, Theorem 10.1

items.statement:
Assume the ultrafilter lemma, dependent choice, and the real Hahn–Banach dominated-extension principle. Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $D\subseteq X$ be nonempty and weakly closed, and let $F:D\to Y$ be a map such that for every sequence $(x_n)$ in $D$ and every $x\in X,z\in Y$, $x_n\rightharpoonup x$ and $F(x_n)\rightharpoonup z$ imply $x\in D$ and $F(x)=z$. Here $D$ is closed in the coarsest topology making every bounded real-linear functional continuous, and weak convergence means convergence under every such functional. For any $\alpha>0$, $x_0\in X$, and $y\in Y$, the nonlinear Tikhonov functional

$$
J_{\alpha,y,x_0}(x)=\frac12\|F(x)-y\|_Y^2+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|x-x_0\|_X^2\qquad(x\in D)
$$

attains a global minimum on $D$; that is, there exists $x_\alpha\in D$ such that $J_{\alpha,y,x_0}(x_\alpha)\le J_{\alpha,y,x_0}(x)$ for every $x\in D$. No exact solution of $F(x)=y$ is required.

items.title: Existence of an $x_0$-minimum-norm exact solution

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems, Chapter 10

items.statement: Assume the ultrafilter lemma, dependent choice, and HB. Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $D\subseteq X$ be nonempty and weakly closed in the coarsest topology making every bounded real-linear functional continuous, and let $F:D\to Y$ satisfy: for every sequence $x_n\in D$ and $x\in X,z\in Y$, if $x_n\rightharpoonup x$ and $F(x_n)\rightharpoonup z$, then $x\in D$ and $F(x)=z$; weak convergence means convergence under every bounded real-linear functional. If $S_F(y):=\{x\in D:F(x)=y\}$ is nonempty for some $y\in Y$, then for every $x_0\in X$ there exists $x^\dagger\in S_F(y)$ such that $\|x^\dagger-x_0\|_X\le\|x-x_0\|_X$ for every $x\in S_F(y)$.

items.title: Weak-cluster stability for fixed-parameter nonlinear Tikhonov regularization

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems, Theorem 10.2

items.statement: Assume the ultrafilter lemma, dependent choice, and HB. Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $D\subseteq X$ be nonempty and weakly closed in the coarsest topology making every bounded real-linear functional continuous, and let $F:D\to Y$ satisfy: whenever $x_n\in D$, $x_n\rightharpoonup x$, and $F(x_n)\rightharpoonup z$, one has $x\in D$ and $F(x)=z$; weak convergence means convergence under every bounded real-linear functional. Fix $\alpha>0$, $x_0\in X$, and $y\in Y$, and let data $y_n\in Y$ satisfy $\|y_n-y\|_Y\to0$. There exists a sequence $(x_n)$ of global minimizers of $J_{\alpha,y_n,x_0}$ on $D$. Every such sequence has a subsequence $x_{n_k}$ with $x_{n_k}\rightharpoonup x$, and every such weak limit $x$ minimizes $J_{\alpha,y,x_0}$ on $D$. No uniqueness of the limiting minimizer is asserted.

items.title: Vanishing-noise convergence to an $x_0$-minimum-norm exact solution

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems, Theorem 10.3

items.statement: Assume the ultrafilter lemma, dependent choice, and HB. Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $D\subseteq X$ be nonempty and weakly closed in the coarsest topology making every bounded real-linear functional continuous, and let $F:D\to Y$ satisfy: whenever $x_n\in D$, $x_n\rightharpoonup x$, and $F(x_n)\rightharpoonup z$, one has $x\in D$ and $F(x)=z$; weak convergence means convergence under every bounded real-linear functional. Fix $x_0\in X$ and suppose $S_F(y^\dagger):=\{x\in D:F(x)=y^\dagger\}$ is nonempty. Let $\delta_n\ge0$, $\delta_n\to0$, $\alpha_n>0$, $\alpha_n\to0$, and $\delta_n^2/\alpha_n\to0$, and let $y_n\in Y$ satisfy $\|y_n-y^\dagger\|_Y\le\delta_n$. There exists a sequence $(x_n)$ of global minimizers of $J_{\alpha_n,y_n,x_0}$ on $D$; every such sequence has a subsequence $x_{n_k}\rightharpoonup x$, and every such weak limit $x$ is an $x_0$-minimum-norm solution of $F(x)=y^\dagger$ on $D$. No uniqueness or full-sequence convergence is asserted.

title: Nonlinear Tikhonov existence and stability — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: A nonlinear Tikhonov functional can have two global minimizers

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems, Chapter 10, nonuniqueness discussion

items.statement:
Let $X=Y=\mathbb R$ with the usual inner product, let $U=\mathbb R$, and define $F:U\to Y$ by $F(t)=t^2$. Take $x_0=0$, $y=1$, and $\alpha=1$. The domain $U$ is weakly closed and, whenever $t_n$ converges weakly to $t$ and $F(t_n)$ converges weakly to $z$, one has $z=F(t)$; weak convergence means convergence under every bounded real-linear functional. The Tikhonov functional is

$$
J(t)=\frac12(t^2-1)^2+\frac12t^2\qquad(t\in\mathbb R).
$$

It has exactly two distinct global minimizers, $t=1/\sqrt2$ and $t=-1/\sqrt2$.

items.title: A Bochner-integral forward map with weakly closed graph
items.statement:
Assume the ultrafilter lemma, dependent choice, and HB. Give $\Omega=\{0,1\}$ its full sigma-algebra and probability measure $\mu(A)=|A|/2$. For each $s\in\mathbb R$, let $g_s:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be the simple function $g_s(0)=s$, $g_s(1)=s^2$, and define $F(s)=\int_\Omega g_s\,d\mu=(s+s^2)/2$. With $X=Y=D=\mathbb R$ and the usual real Hilbert structure, $D$ is weakly closed and $F$ is nonlinear; if $s_n\rightharpoonup s$ and $F(s_n)\rightharpoonup z$, then $z=F(s)$, where weak convergence in $\mathbb R$ means convergence under every bounded real-linear functional. For every $\alpha>0$, $x_0,y\in\mathbb R$, its Tikhonov functional

$$
J_{\alpha,y,x_0}(s)=\frac12|F(s)-y|^2+\frac{\alpha}{2}|s-x_0|^2
$$

has a global minimizer on $\mathbb R$.
